Q: search a single word in a column A:

First, sanitize user input. Never query the database directly from the user input, as this may cause SQL Injection.

After sanatizing the user input, try using the LIKE function.

For example:

SELECT 'Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Buffet, Snack' LIKE '%Lunch%' would output 1.

SELECT 'Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Buffet, Snack' LIKE '%NonExistantCategory%' would output 0.

Try changing your query to SELECT * FROM restaurants WHERE category LIKE '%$searchinfoSanatized%', where $searchinfoSanatized is the input that has been filtered/escaped.

Also, I believe you are forgetting a - after RestoModel: $restaurantinfo['restaurantinfo']=$this->RestoModel>searchRestaurant($searchinfo);

Q: Why does the dash command `test -d` without the file arg pass without error? A:

This is documented in POSIX spec for test as follows:

The algorithm for determining the precedence of the operators and the return value that shall be generated is based on the number of arguments presented to test.

In the following list, $1, $2, $3, and $4 represent the arguments presented to test:

0 arguments:

Exit false (1).

1 argument:

Exit true (0) if $1 is not null; otherwise, exit false.

2 arguments:

  • If $1 is '!', exit true if $2 is null, false if $2 is not null.

  • If $1 is a unary primary, exit true if the unary test is true, false if the unary test is false.

There is only one argument in test -d and it is not null, -d is only considered a binary operator when there is an argument next to it. You can do test -d "$9" (with double quotes) to make sure test is called with two arguments even when $9 is empty or unset.

Q: Data structure for large set of stepwise/incremental data and method to store it A:

You are managing a row of building structures with varying heights represented by an array structures. You want to transform these structures into a harmonious pattern where each structure differs from its adjacent neighbors by exactly one unit in height, forming either an ascending or descending sequence.

To modify the structures, you can only add one unit of height to any structure in a single operation. Your goal is to determine the minimum number of operations needed to achieve either an ascending or descending stepwise pattern - whichever requires fewer operations.

Example

•

For structures = [1, 4, 3, 2], the output should be solution(structures) = 4.

The optimal approach is to add:

o

Four units to the first structure.

The final heights will be: [5, 4, 3, 2], forming a descending stepwise pattern.

•

For structures = [5, 7, 9, 4, 11], the output should be solution(structures) = 9.

The optimal approach is to add:

o

Two units to the first structure;

o

One unit to the second structure;

o

Six units to the fourth structure.

The final heights will be: [7, 8, 9, 10, 11], forming an ascending stepwise pattern.

Input/Output

•

[execution time limit] 4 seconds (py)

•

[memory limit] 1 GB

•

[input] array.integer structures

An array of integers representing the height of each structure.

Guaranteed constraints: 2 ≤ structures.length ≤ 105, 1 ≤ structures[i] ≤ 109.

•

[output] integer64

Return the minimum number of operations required to create either an ascending or descending stepwise pattern - whichever requires fewer operations.

Q: Message data of MSI-X is useless, right? A:

It's not useless, it's just not data that you can use for IO. The data in the "message data" field identifies which interrupt is being requested just like in MSI. To send an interrupt you have to send that specific data to that specific address.

"But, in MSI-X, we have different Message address for different vectors" -- that's not true. In MSI-X, each device interrupt has a specified address and data programmed by the host into the devices MSI-X configuration table. A given host could use a separate address for each interrupt and ignore the data, or it could have a single address and use the data field. If there was a specific "intent" behind the rules it is that each processor would have an interrupt controller at a different address. The data field would still be used to send the interrupt request number, and the address is for selecting which CPU to route it to.

As mentioned by Theodore the Xilinx PCIe bridge (and other PCIe bridges I have seen) require you to supply the MSI-X address and data when you send an interrupt, while for MSI they only require the local interrupt index in the range 0..31. However, this is not a license to send arbitrary data! These fields must be set exactly based on the MSI-X configuration table programmed by the host during device enumeration.

Q: Why is my body element smaller than my html element? A:

The only way I could get rid of the 8-pixel body margin was the nuclear option from https://www.miriamsuzanne.com/2022/07/04/body-margin-8px/: * {all: initial !important; }

But then I found out it was because I had a separate body { ... } rule after the html, body {margin: 0; ... } rule, and the latter was causing Firefox to ignore the former. Swapped the order and got rid of the 8-pixel margin.
